formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.EncodedColorParameterData.reads {μ : ℕ → ℤ} {params n : ℕ} (H : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Seg μ params (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightParameterInit.values n)) :
    μ params=(_root_.ThreeSum.Scales.inputBits n : ℤ) ∧ μ (params+1)=(_root_.ThreeSum.Scales.microHalf (_root_.ThreeSum.Scales.inputBits n) : ℤ) ∧
    μ (params+3)=(_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.Scales.blockCount (_root_.ThreeSum.Scales.inputBits n) : ℤ) ∧ μ (params+4)=(_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.Scales.mu n : ℤ) ∧
    μ (params+14)=(_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.Scales.radix n : ℤ) ∧ μ (params+17)=(_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BandScales.bandSize n : ℤ) ∧
    μ (params+18)=(_root_.ThreeSum.Scales.primeWindow n : ℤ) := by sorry
natural_language_statement:
If the segment at parameter base $p$ contains initializer values for input length $n$, offsets $0,1,3,4,14,17,18$ contain respectively the bit count, micro-half size, block count, total block size, radix, band size, and prime-window size.

These read equations connect parameter-header RAM expressions to the exact integer schedule used in later contracts.
